title: Trumpet soloists: George McCullum
summary: George McCullum was the outstanding trumpet soloist for hymns and dirges, a clean player who did not blast.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Did they have anybody who was outstanding for trumpet solos?

Yeah. George McCulloch. That's one of the guys that nobody did 90 years ago. They used to fit him all the time. Any hot thing coming, the King Madras and things. They didn't come back. The boy gets back. He's been a little bit further. He's been trouble with that.
Would he specialize in funeral directors?
Anything. Anything. Concerts. Anything. We speak all of them.
Like Pajo today. Now that's what Pajo liked to do best is play a solo on the 3rd it seems
Because he'd rather play a funeral than eat a turkey dinner.

Well, me too. I would see my man when I was there. I'd be so glad I'd jump with that. I'd be the first and the first and the first job. I used to love it and I loved it up until long but I know I can't pay more for him. Because if a fellow can do a job and do it good, he makes it. That's between me. I know. I know. I didn't need nobody to tell them. But when I was there, I was going to go to the other. And then when they get up there, I'd be the first man out of it too. I'd get my first person every trip. Even though we know it.
Any other men that specialize in hims and durians other than McCollum?
Well, I think he was doing that. And he was the best around him. And at that time, he did. I think he was the best. And then Mr. Ithlap, he used to be pretty good too. Lionel Faber.
I'm trying to think about the different guys I've heard about his being good at Fennells. Alvin Alcorn played beautiful with Ole Manol and some. And Manuel Parage is supposed to have been good.

Oh, yeah. He was good. He was strong and everything. But you see, this boy, McCollum, he didn't blast nothing. But the tune came out and he said, he just as clear as anything. He didn't blast nothing. Of course, as a matter of fact, he was a strong man on the track. He didn't blast. But the other boy, McCollum, he didn't blast. I swore it to him. But you could hear it anyway. I see.
